_docs: Definition of Done per completeness tier (task #8). Edit freely; the adherence gate grades the built app against the ACTIVE tier's checklist, and designlint enforces the machine-checkable items. Tiers inherit: mvp includes prototype's items, v1 includes mvp's, production_draft includes v1's.
_functionality_rule: BINDING at every tier, checked first: the app is NOT a cosmetic prototype. A screen that LOOKS finished but whose controls don't actually work (taps that do nothing, fake/hardcoded data instead of real state, calculations not performed, nothing persisted) is UNMET regardless of visual polish. Looking done and being done are graded separately; only being done counts.
prototype: Every core feature in the prompt/requirements is FUNCTIONALLY implemented, not just visually present: real logic runs, real data is produced/stored, real state changes persist across navigation and relaunch where the feature implies it should.
The primary user workflow works end-to-end (create/see/act on the core object) using REAL data entered by the user, not hardcoded placeholder content standing in for it.
The app launches to a real screen, not a placeholder.
No crash on the primary workflow.
mvp: Every screen has empty, loading, and error states — not just the happy path.
Dark mode is styled (both palettes from the design handoff, readable).
Onboarding or a self-explanatory first screen exists.
All views style through DesignSystem tokens (no inline colors/fonts).
Every interactive element has an accessibilityIdentifier.
v1: All declared user flows (flows.json) pass against the built app.
No TODO/FIXME markers left in source.
Settings/preferences screen exists where the prompt implies configurability.
App icon and display name are set.
production_draft: Unit or UI test target exists and runs.
Accessibility audit issues addressed (labels, contrast, dynamic type).
No dead buttons (every tappable does something).
